data.title: Decoding the PI3K/Akt/mTOR-JAK/STAT signaling axis in multiple sclerosis: mechanistic crosstalk and therapeutic opportunities.
data.authors: Banerjee C; Singh RK; Choudhary D; Khan MN; Maurya PK; Khan Z et al.

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Review mapping the mechanistic crosstalk between PI3K/Akt/mTOR and JAK/STAT pathways in MS neuroinflammation, identifying dual-pathway mTOR targeting as a therapeutic opportunity to reduce immune dysregulation and demyelination.
data.abstract_excerpt: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated neurodegenerative disorder characterized by demyelination, axonal injury, and progressive neurological dysfunction. Emerging evidence identifies PI3K/Akt/mTOR and JAK/STAT pathways as interconnected regulators of neuroinflammation and immune dysregulation in MS.

extracted_findings.effect: PI3K/Akt/mTOR-JAK/STAT crosstalk drives neuroinflammation in MS; mTOR inhibition proposed as treatment
